error_direction_rationale: A schedule that would otherwise violate a declared rule refuses by name instead of computing: a benchmark or hybrid basis with no floor and cap, a schedule with no takaful protection, a non-default wa'd trigger and a rental revision without mutual agreement all return structured refusals. Rentals are exact BigInt products with round-half-even per month, and a benchmark-determined component is clamped into the declared bounds, so a computed row cannot silently exceed the declared ceiling.

branches.branch: The rental is determined and agreed by the contracting parties at the inception of the ijarah contract; the schedule derives every month from inception-declared inputs only.
The rental amount may be a fixed amount.
The rental amount may be determined via reference to a specified benchmark or formula.
The rental amount may combine a fixed part with a benchmark-determined part.
A benchmark-determined rental is subject to a minimum and a maximum limit; every benchmark-determined component is clamped into the declared bounds.
A benchmark-determined rental without both a floor and a cap cannot be scheduled.
The lessor must not increase the rental unilaterally; a rental revision record without a declared mutual agreement is refused.
The contracting parties may mutually agree to revise the rental; revisions with a declared mutual agreement are applied to the named months.
Rights and liabilities arising from ownership of the leased asset sit with the lessor and are shown as lessor lines in the schedule.
Expenses of maintaining the availability and accessibility of the usufruct are borne by the lessor and appear as a per-month lessor line.

The lessee is liable for loss, damage or impairment of the leased asset unless the absence of misconduct, negligence or breach of terms on the lessee's part is proven; the caller declares which branch applies.

assumption_of_use.value: lessee_fault, the proven-fact declaration of the loss branch
assumption_of_use.source: the caller's own factual determination external to this node
assumption_of_use.owner: the caller supplying the total-loss inputs

branches.branch: Where the loss is proven due to the lessee's misconduct, negligence or breach, the lessee bears restoration and remains liable for rent during restoration.

The contracting parties may mutually agree on who bears the cost of maintenance and takaful protection; the node always shows the cost lines as lessor lines and does not model the agreed reallocation.

assumption_of_use.value: maintenance_minor_units_per_month as a lessor-borne line per the ownership default
assumption_of_use.source: the caller's own ijarah contract terms external to this node
assumption_of_use.owner: the caller declaring the cost lines

branches.branch: Where impairment without proven lessee fault occurs, the lessor restores the usufruct and bears the cost; rent stops from the loss month.
The lessor must obtain takaful protection for the leased asset; a schedule with no takaful line and no declared exception is refused.
The conventional-insurance exception applies only when no takaful line is declared; declaring both is refused.
The leased asset may be protected through conventional insurance where the declared circumstance applies: not offered, rejected by all operators, or significantly more competitive cost.
A declared conventional-insurance circumstance without an insurance cost line is refused rather than scheduled unprotected.
The contract ends with the lessee owning the asset via sale, conditional hibah or wa'd to hibah; the transfer mode is a required declared input echoed with its execution semantics.
A sale transfer is executed as a separate contract after expiry or termination of the ijarah contract, at a declared transfer price.
A conditional hibah becomes effective once the relevant condition is fulfilled; the condition itself is a contract fact outside the values-only input set.

assumption_of_use.value: the fulfilment state of the hibah condition
assumption_of_use.source: the caller's ijarah contract documentation external to this node

branches.branch: A wa'd to hibah executes the hibah as a contract separate from the ijarah contract.
At inception the lessor may request a wa'd to purchase the leased asset; a declared trigger is echoed on the transfer event.
The wa'd may be triggered only by an event of default or a breach of the wa'd documentation terms; any other claimed trigger is refused.
Only the pinned Malaysian regulator profile is supported; any other authority is refused by name instead of borrowing its numbers.
Rental may be paid in advance or deferred and received in advance; the node schedules monthly rentals due in arrears only and does not model advance or deferred payment timing.
The adequacy of the takaful cover relative to the asset value is not assessed; the takaful line is a caller-declared cost amount only.
